# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Start with your revenue anchors, not your offerings:**
Audit last 3 months of transactions—which services actually generate repeat revenue? Which attract new members? Build your menu around *what sells*, not what you think should sell. This tells you pricing power too.

**Create two separate documents (not one confused hybrid):**
- **Coach version**: Decision tree (IF member asks X, THEN offer Y), pricing tiers they can quote, what they can/can't bundle. Laminate it. They need to memorize this in week one.
- **Member version**: Clean pricing page (digital + printed). Lead with your most popular/profitable service, bury the cheap options. Include "package vs. pay-as-you-go" comparison so members self-select.

**Price by perceived outcome, not time spent:**
Don't say "6-week program £150." Say "Results-guaranteed 6-week strength program—£150 (vs. £15/drop-in cost = better value)." This justifies premium pricing and filters for committed members.

**Do a 48-hour soft launch:**
Send the draft menu to 5-10 loyal members + your coaches. Ask ONE question: "What's confusing?" You'll catch pricing contradictions and unclear language before it goes live—saves you from re-doing this in 3 weeks.

**Lock it in a shared document your coaches access daily:**
Google Sheet or Notion (not email). Version-dated. Updates go there first. Coaches must see pricing changes before members do.

What's your current biggest revenue driver—personal training sessions, group classes, or memberships?

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## REVENUE — CRITICAL PRIORITY

**Single biggest issue: Revenue/member has collapsed.** Oct £105 vs Sep £138 (–24%), Aug £106 (–23%). You're adding members (169 vs 160) but extracting far less per head. This signals:

- **Audit your pricing mix NOW.** Sep's £138/member suggests a blend of full-price and discounted memberships. Oct dropped to £105 — either a cohort of new members joined on intro rates, or class packs/cards underperformed. Pull your GoCardless + Stripe breakdown by product (monthly membership vs pay-as-you-go cards). If >40% of active members are on sub-£15/month intro rates, you're building a low-margin base. Harden pricing: retire intro offers after 3 months or cap them to <15% of intake.

- **Churn spiked May (12.8%), then stabilized 3–6%.** Sep–Oct holding at 6.2% → 4.0% is good, but you're still losing 1 in 16 members monthly. This is eating growth. Target: <3%. Run exit surveys (TeamUp has exit tags) and identify the three reasons people leave. Odds are: class timetable mismatch, new competitor, or feeling invisible. Plug the biggest leak first (likely cost <£500 to fix).

- **Fill quiet classes with dynamic pricing.** Sep's revenue spike (£22k, 160 members) came on 9 extra members but +£5.2k revenue vs Aug — this is pricing + utilization working. Identify your lowest-attended off-peak slots (likely early morning or Mon/Fri late evening). Offer flash discounts (48-hour email: "Monday 6pm spin is 20% off this week — book now") to existing members only, no free passes. Expect 30–40% uptake; margin is still positive vs empty room.

---

## EXPENSES — WHERE TO LOOK

- **Sep–Oct cash burn not visible, but revenue drop suggests margin pressure.** Last 3 months avg £18.6k revenue; prior 3 months (Jun–Aug, excluding relocation month) avg £17.3k. You've grown top line +7.5%, but member revenue *down* 23%. **Your fixed costs (rent, insurance, utilities post-relocation) are now spread thinner.** Pull your P&L for Sep and Oct: what's your contribution margin (revenue minus class instructor wages + utilities)? If it's <55%, you're in trouble
